question: As per the 2025 Human Development Index (HDI) report, what is India's HDI value for 2023 that places it in the medium human development category?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.685**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**. It measures the social and economic development of countries based on three major dimensions: **health, education,** and **standard of living**.
 
• **India's HDI Value:** As per the **2025 Human Development Index report**, India's HDI value for **2023** is **0.685**, which positions the country in the **medium human development category**.
 
• **Global Ranking:** India's HDI value places it among countries striving to achieve significant progress in human development. It shows **improvements in life expectancy, education levels, and income per capita**.
 
• **Medium Human Development Category:** Countries with HDI values between **0.55** and **0.7** are classified under the medium human development category. India's position reflects the **ongoing efforts to balance economic growth and social development**.
 
• **Development Challenges:** Despite improvements, India still faces challenges in areas such as **reducing inequality, improving healthcare infrastructure, and enhancing education quality**, which are critical to achieving higher HDI rankings in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of HDI:**

 
 
• **Health:** Measured by **life expectancy at birth**, it reflects the ability to live a long and healthy life.
 
• **Education:** Calculated using **mean years of schooling** (average schooling received by people aged 25 and older) and **expected years of schooling** (schooling a child entering the education system is expected to receive).
 
• **Standard of Living:** Assessed using **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP).
 
 
 
• **UNDP and HDI:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** introduced the HDI in **1990**, aiming to emphasize that people and their capabilities should be the ultimate criteria for assessing the development of a country.
 
• It is published annually in the **Human Development Report**.
 
 
 
• **India's HDI Progress:**
 
 
• India has consistently improved its HDI score over the years due to programs aimed at reducing poverty, enhancing education, and improving healthcare services.
 
• Government initiatives such as **Ayushman Bharat, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao,** and **Skill India** play a critical role in boosting India's socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Countries:**
 
 
• Countries with an HDI above **0.8** are classified as having **high human development**. For instance, **Norway** consistently ranks high due to its robust healthcare system, quality education, and high income levels.
 
• India, with its HDI of **0.685**, ranks lower than countries like **China (0.768)** but higher than countries in the **low human development** category such as **Niger (0.394)**.
 
 
 
• **Human Development Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite progress, challenges such as **income inequality, gender disparity, and rural-urban divides** continue to affect India's development trajectory.
 
• Addressing these issues is essential for India to transition into the high human development category in the future.
